display_name: Osa-AK battery: march, short halt, combat formation and halts
status: Numbers for simcore/battery.hpp (roadmap 7.5). The tactics are the Soviet 1991 textbook's (voenizdat_osa_1991 chapter 6, pp. 231-239, tier 1, for the Osa-AKM battery), which confirms the unnamed manual retold in video_osa (tier 4) on nearly every point; docs/research/OSA_MANUALS_2026-10.md. Where a range is given, the middle is used unless noted; speeds are from the manuals.
notes: Composition: flak11 (Osa-AK: the battery commander's PU-12M, two platoons of two 9A33 and one TZM, a maintenance vehicle); voenizdat_osa_1991 p226 (Osa-AKM: command, control section, four launcher crews, a MANPADS section, a supply section, a maintenance crew; PU-12M, four 9A33BM3, three MANPADS launchers, two TZM, the 9V210M3 maintenance vehicle and the ZIP-2 vehicle). Ambush and roving tasks (p238: a position, a sector, a route, rules for search and fire, a time to leave) and the river crossing (p237: positions 2-3 km from the river; across swimming in pairs behind the first-echelon battalions once their bridgeheads are 1.6-2 km deep) are the textbook's.

march_spacing_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p232 (25-50 m between vehicles in the column); video_osa agrees

threat_spacing_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p232 (at least 200 m between the launchers when an air attack is to be met from short halts; the column then 700-800 m deep); video_osa (200-800 m)

march_speed_mps.source: mon_2112_80 p11, voenizdat_osa_1991 p16 (dirt roads 30 km/h; road up to 60); korovin_tiv_2010 (dirt roads 36 km/h by day, 25 at night): 30 km/h for a column

short_halt_offset_m.source: mon_2112_80 p66 (a target found beyond 20 km: pull 30-50 m off the road); voenizdat_osa_1991 p233, p254 (the launcher leaves the roadway; beyond 20 km to the side away from the target, within 20 km it stops in the column)

short_halt_in_column_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p254 (a target within 20 km: stop without leaving the column; beyond it, leave the column to the side away from the target); mon_2112_80 p66 (the same 20 km)
short_halt_in_column_m.notes: A short halt ordered with the target's position: inside this range every vehicle stops in its place on the road; beyond it each pulls off to the side away from the target. Without a target the vehicles alternate sides.

deploy_s.source: mon_2112_80 p11-12, voenizdat_osa_1991 p16 (march to combat within 4 min, the gas-turbine start included): used for an NPC vehicle
deploy_s.notes: voenizdat_osa_1991 p231 gives the battery 35-50 s into combat order and 15-30 s back into march order: a battery marching with its equipment on (video_osa says the same).

pair_separation_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p234-237 (pairs up to 3 km apart, so their zones overlap, dead cones included); video_osa agrees

pair_internal_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p234, p237 (at least 200 m within a pair, up to 500 m; no mutual interference); video_osa agrees

behind_covered_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p234, p237 (1.5-3 km behind the covered companies' leading line); video_osa agrees

reload_behind_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p234 (the TZM crews within 500 m of the launchers); video_osa agrees

command_post_behind_m.source: estimate; voenizdat_osa_1991 p234, p237 (the battery command post at the centre of the battle order or near a pair; its PU-12M follows the launchers at a distance that keeps control steady; on the march at the head of the column, p239)

halt_interval_s.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p238 (a halt every 3-4 h of movement: checks, faults, maintenance, fuel, rest); video_osa agrees

halt_duration_s.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p238 (halts of up to 1 h; one of up to 2 h for a meal in the second half of the day's march, not modelled)
halt_duration_s.notes: Was 1.5 h from video_osa's 'up to 2 h'.

night_halt_s.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p238-239 (halts of up to 1 h without breaking the column's order; marches best by night); video_osa (at night about 1 h)

warning_s.source: flak11 (preliminary preparation from cold: 3.8 min switch-on and 3.0 min function check, 6.8 min)
warning_s.notes: The warning the launchers need: the NPC battery commander raises readiness when the board shows a track that will reach the edge of the zone in this time or less (simcore/board_reading.hpp). Without a speed (one mark) the threat range below decides. voenizdat_osa_1991 p251: the function check must not delay opening fire.

zone_edge_m.source: flak11 (Osa-AK engagement zone head-on to 10 km); voenizdat_osa_1991 p15 (10-10.3 km)
zone_edge_m.notes: Where the warning time is counted to: the far edge of the launchers' zone, from the battery.

threat_range_m.source: samsim_osa p21 (the crew waits until a target approaches the 50 km circle): a designated target inside this makes the battery open the column (sam3d)

water_speed_mps.source: mon_2112_80 p11, voenizdat_osa_1991 p16, flak11 (9K33-0), nuou (8 km/h in water)

river_standoff_m.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p237 (the battery's positions 2-3 km from the river); video_osa (about 2 km)

ambush_dwell_s.source: estimate (voenizdat_osa_1991 p238 gives an ambush or roving launcher a time to leave each position, not its length)

alongside_offset_m.source: estimate (the TZM parks beside the launcher, its crane over the containers: flak11)

tzm_capacity.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p188 (the 9T217BM2 carries 1 to 12 missiles, six a side; loads a launcher in 5-8 min)

fuel_truck_capacity_l.source: estimate (an ATZ-3.8 tanker: 3.8 m3 by its designation)
